### Observed differences

- The elapsed time between consecutive completion events for the A26–A18 transition roughly halved: in the earlier window these gaps averaged about 0.9 hours (median about 0.93; the middle half fell between about 0.83 and 0.99 hours), while in the later window they averaged about 0.46 hours (median about 0.46; the middle half fell between about 0.41 and 0.51 hours) — a difference of about 0.45 hours. [TWAIT001]
- The gaps also became more consistent, with the spread narrowing from a standard deviation of about 0.13 hours to about 0.08 hours. [TWAIT001]
- This comparison rests on 47 observed gaps in each window (out of 200 traces per window), and the difference is larger than in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits of the pooled traces, so it is unusual for an unchanged process — though this is not the probability that a change occurred. [TWAIT001]
- Note that this indicator measures elapsed time between consecutive completion events, not pure waiting, service or processing time. [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a structural change in the process. Only one evidence item was found where about 0.4 items would be expected by chance in an unchanged process — a count an unchanged process typically produces — and a shorter elapsed time between consecutive completions of A26 and A18 does not show which structural element, if any, changed. [TWAIT001]

Schema: pcr-evidence-2.1. Windows: 200 traces before, 200 after. Screening: 82 units tested, 0.41 items expected without change.

Evidence: one item, TWAIT001. T_WAIT indicator between consecutive completion events, for the pair/transition involving activities A26 and A18 (analysis_unit values ["A26", "A18"]). Wasserstein distance in hours: observed_change 0.449 hours. Before: mean 0.905 hours (about 0.9 h), median 0.93, q25 0.83, q75 0.99, std 0.13, count 47. After: mean 0.456 hours, median 0.46, q25 0.41, q75 0.51, std 0.08, count 47. So the elapsed time between consecutive completion events for this transition roughly halved: from about 0.9 hours to about 0.46 hours. Empirical strength 0.995 — the difference is larger than in 99.5% of random re-splits. Support: 47 observations in each window (out of 200 traces each).

Judging support: First compare number of evidence items (1) with items_expected_without_change (0.41). One item when fewer than one is expected — "A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces: choose 'Insufficient evidence', however large or unusual a single item looks."

So: 1 item vs 0.41 expected — same order of magnitude. Therefore: Insufficient evidence.

Also, the hypothesis type: a time change (T_WAIT) is not a structural change indicator per se. The instructions say a hypothesis about order or placement needs relational/positional evidence. A time decrease alone doesn't directly show a structural change. Even if we wanted a hypothesis, TWAIT is elapsed time between consecutive completion events; a halving of elapsed time between A26 and A18 completions doesn't directly establish a structural change (could be caused by many things, and structural change hypotheses need direct structural evidence).

So the answer:

### Observed differences
- The elapsed time between consecutive completion events involving A26 and A18 decreased: in the earlier window, the gap between these consecutive completions averaged about 0.9 hours (median about 0.93 hours, middle half roughly 0.83–0.99 hours); in the later window it averaged about 0.46 hours (median about 0.46, middle half roughly 0.41–0.51). That is roughly a halving, a difference of about 0.45 hours. [TWAIT001]
- The gap was based on 47 observations in each window (out of 200 traces each), and the difference is larger than in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits of the pooled data, so it is unusual for a random split. [TWAIT001]
- Note: TWAIT is elapsed time between consecutive completion events, not pure waiting/service time.

Also mention variability decreased (std from 0.13 to 0.08).

### Inference
Support level: Insufficient evidence
"The evidence is insufficient to infer a structural change in the process." Add one short sentence on limitation: only one item was found where about 0.41 would be expected by chance in an unchanged process, and a timing change alone does not show which structure changed.
